structure_tensor_orientation — 2D texture op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "structure_tensor_orientation", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The output is shown in a viridis-like pseudo-colour (dark purple = low, yellow = high) so that a field of quantities — distance, phase, orientation, depth — can be read.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ structure_tensor_orientation: knob a sweep (docs site)

Sweeping knob b (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ structure_tensor_orientation: knob b sweep (docs site)

On other images (synthetic scene / photo / coins. Top row: inputs, bottom row: their outputs. Knobs at default):

▸ structure_tensor_orientation: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Returns the local direction in which stripes run (principal axis of the structure tensor) mapped to [0,1].

0 and 1 both correspond to horizontal and 0.5 to vertical (orientation wraps around every 180 degrees, so 0 and 1 are the same orientation — note that differencing this output produces false steps at the seam).

a is the pre-derivative smoothing sigma (0.5-3.0 pixels), b the integration window rho (1.0-8.0 pixels). rho is "over how wide an area the orientation is considered aligned"; take it larger than the pitch of fibres or polishing marks.

Conditions of use: orientation can be defined only where the gradient is structurally biased. Pixels where the tensor's anisotropy is below 1e-6 relative to the trace (flat surfaces, isotropic noise) return 0.5 as "orientation undefined" — without a floor here, rounding dust on a uniform surface is amplified by arctan2 and changing the brightness by just 0.01 flips the orientation everywhere at once. Measure the reliability of the orientation separately with structure_tensor_coherence.

Uses: fibre orientation in fibre-reinforced materials, direction of rolling and polishing striations, wood grain, elongation direction of crystal grains. HALCON has no corresponding standalone op.
